reading.body:
Accounting AI has moved from vendor claims to measured adoption and full-population audit testing, with professional bodies setting guidance.

The sources span professional guidance, direct firm surveys, independent benchmarks, and audit platforms. AICPA and AICPA-CIMA maintain the profession's direction on audit use and risk, while IMA covers corporate finance and CFO organizations. Census BTOS reports professional-services AI use directly from firms, so adoption is measured rather than guessed. Vals AI benchmarks financial reasoning on corporate finance and tax tasks by accuracy, not vendor claims.

The structural change is in audit. MindBridge and similar platforms score every general-ledger entry rather than a sample, replacing sampling with full-population testing. Transaction classification, anomaly detection, and close automation are the working uses. This data does not cover compute, power, or building constraints, and it gives no adoption rates, accuracy scores, or cost figures.

summary: Transaction classification, anomaly detection in audit, and close automation are the working uses.
